publicly_readable: The editor's letter (ten trends) in full, via an Internet Archive snapshot taken two days after publication.
not_readable: The body text of the other articles (paywalled), the 'Wild cards' section, 'Trendlines' and the forecast tables. The self-review of 2025 predictions, if The Economist published one in The World Ahead 2026, was not found in public form.

entries.quote: Mr Trump may push Ukraine to do a deal with Russia and give Israel a free hand in its conflicts in Gaza and Lebanon.
entries.subject: Ukraine-Russia deal under US pressure

entries.quote: For now, America’s rivalry with China will manifest itself as a trade war, as Mr Trump imposes restrictions and ramps up tariffs—including on America’s allies.
entries.subject: US tariffs on China and allies

entries.quote: In America, Mr Trump’s policies will make things worse: hefty import tariffs could hamper growth and reignite inflation.
entries.subject: US inflation after tariffs

entries.quote: The backlash against “overtourism” will diminish in 2025, but restrictions introduced by many cities, from Amsterdam to Venice, will remain.
entries.subject: Overtourism backlash and city restrictions

notes: The letter is mostly themes. The 2025 edition is the 39th (counting back from the 40th in 2026).
